definitions.explanation: The act of separating a person or thing from others. Used in medical contexts for quarantine, and more broadly for any forced separation or segregation.

examples.japanese: {感染者|かんせんしゃ}は{隔離|かくり}された。
{隔離|かくり}{期間|きかん}は{五日間|いつかかん}だった。
examples.english: The quarantine period was five days.

examples.japanese: {新型|しんがた}ウイルスの{感染|かんせん}{拡大|かくだい}を{防|ふせ}ぐため、{濃厚|のうこう}{接触者|せっしょくしゃ}は{自宅|じたく}で{隔離|かくり}された。
examples.english: To prevent the spread of the new virus, close contacts were quarantined at home.

notes:
Compound of {隔|かく} (to separate/partition) + {離|り} (to detach/distance). Carries a clinical or official tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隔離|かくり}する (to isolate; to quarantine)
- {隔離|かくり}{期間|きかん} (quarantine period)
- {隔離|かくり}{施設|しせつ} (quarantine facility)
- {隔離|かくり}{病棟|びょうとう} (isolation ward)
- {自宅|じたく}{隔離|かくり} (home quarantine)

USAGE NOTE:
Became widely known during the COVID-19 pandemic. Also used historically for the forced segregation of people with diseases such as Hansen's disease (leprosy).
